# Psalm 57 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. According to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul, in the cave.

**2** Be merciful to me, O God, be merciful to me, for in You my soul takes refuge; in the shadow of Your wings I will take refuge, till the storms of destruction pass by.

**3** I cry out to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me.

**4** He will send from heaven and save me; He will put to shame him who tramples on me. Selah. God will send out His steadfast love and His faithfulness!

**5** My soul is in the midst of lions; I lie down amid fiery beasts — the children of man, whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.

**6** Be exalted, O God, above the heavens! Let Your glory be over all the earth!

**7** They set a net for my steps; my soul was bowed down. They dug a pit in my way, but they have fallen into it themselves. Selah.

**8** My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast! I will sing and make melody!

**9** Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn!

**10** I will give thanks to You, O Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises to You among the nations.

**11** For Your steadfast love is great to the heavens, Your faithfulness to the clouds.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 57.

- **57:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **57:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **57:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **57:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **57:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **57:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **57:9**: 'I will awaken the dawn' — the psalmist doesn't wait for morning; he summons it with music. Praise anticipates deliverance.

### LOGOS
- **57:1**: The cave (1 Samuel 22 or 24) — a place of hiding becomes a place of worship. Even in the cave, David's heart is 'steadfast.'

### PNEUMA
- **57:7-8**: The dramatic pivot: from lions and traps (vv.4-7a) to steadfast confidence and dawn-waking music (vv.7b-9). The cave becomes a concert hall.

— SOPHIA
